# Immersive frontend UI — Awwwards-grade landing pages and motion systems

Curated by Skill Harbor — a skill from the awesome-copilot collection (by Utkarsh Patrikar, MIT) that pushes an AI engineering assistant past functional HTML/CSS into architecting immersive digital environments. When a user asks for a premium landing page or portfolio, the skill imposes six disciplines: a creative foundation (commit to a visual identity — editorial brutalism, organic fluidity, cyber/technical, cinematic pacing), structural requirements (preloaders, full-bleed hero architecture with syntactic typography chunking, contextual scroll-reactive navigation), a motion design system (scroll-driven pinned containers and horizontal journeys, magnetic components, custom cursors, transform-only animation), premium typography and texture (fluid type scales, variable fonts, grain overlays, frosted glass), a performance imperative (GPU-composited properties only, reduced-motion and touch degradation, strict guardrails), and a framework ecosystem (Framer Motion/Lenis/React Three Fiber for React, GSAP/Lenis/SplitType for vanilla/Astro). MIT-licensed. Honest caveats: it is taste-and-opinion heavy — results reflect one author's aesthetic doctrine, so adapt the identity to your brand; premium motion costs real engineering effort and can hurt accessibility if the reduced-motion rules are skipped; heavy animation stacks can be rough on low-end devices. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
